changeNote: If your home has a corner that sticks out at the North-East, the North or the East, your score has gone up. We were counting that against you, and we should not have been. A part sticking out at the North-East is the most fortunate shape this tradition recognises — your own report has always said so in the paragraph about a missing North-East corner, while the number underneath it did the opposite. The corner is still shown to you; it simply no longer counts as a fault. A corner sticking out at the South-West, South-East or North-West is unchanged, because those are the ones the tradition really does warn about. Nothing has been removed from your report.
